chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from A'iz al-Ahmasi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I wanted to ask him about the night prayer. So I said, 'Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'And upon you be peace. Yes, by Allah, we are indeed his sons, and we are not merely his relatives' — he said this three times. Then he said, without me asking him: 'When you meet Allah having performed the five obligatory prayers, He will not ask you about anything besides that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the five obligatory prayers in meeting Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, A'iz al-Ahmasi visits Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to ask about the merits of night prayer (*Salat al-Layl*), to which the Imam responds that strict adherence to the five obligatory prayers ensures one is not questioned about other voluntary acts. This highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the *Fara'id* (obligations) are the primary criterion for divine accountability, serving as the foundation upon which *Sunnah* (voluntary acts) are built. The Imam’s triple emphasis on their status underscores the gravity of fulfilling these core duties as the gateway to Paradise.
